assumptions: The clinician-facing endpoints are the three in the app group: patients/{patient_id} GET, clinical_notes POST, appointments GET
Appointments GET being public was unintended, so adding auth is in scope under the approved plan
The debug.log on $input[""] was an accidental leftover, so removing it is in scope
phi as a tag name and phi_access_log as a table name are free in the workspace (dry-run reported no conflict)
$auth is available inside log_phi_access when called from logged-in endpoints
confusions: The skill says the policy file lives at policies/<KEY>.xs under the project root; the brief says ./workspace/policies/<KEY>.xs. I followed the brief.

The skill's sensitive-field and table-tag syntax in XanoScript is not documented in the skill or catalogue. I guessed {sensitive = true} on schema fields and tags = ["phi"] in the table block. The dry-run accepted both (UPDATE_FIELD / UPDATE), but I have not confirmed the output matches what Studio writes.

Recipe says CONF-010 takes table_tags only, but also says a function is required for the access rule. It is split into a separate statement_required rule, which is not a catalogue template. The skill does not say whether that split is expected.
Field-name checks take bare names with no table scope, so shared names (email, phone, note, reason) cannot be targeted. The catalogue does not say how to target one table's field.
Parse warned that phi and phi_access_log are not in the workspace. That is expected for new names, but the warning text does not say whether names in the same change are checked together.
wished_for: A table/field scope param for table.field_attribute_required and table.tag_required, so bare names do not hit other tables.
An example of XanoScript field attributes (sensitive) and table tags in the policies topic.
A recipe that says which templates to skip when a vendor list is unknown, with a placeholder-free option.
Guidance on whether appointments GET being public should be treated as a bug or a choice.
why_confidence: The enforcement is wired (access log, function, unconditional call, login, sensitive marking, phi tags), and the dry run accepted all objects and the policy. Confidence is only medium because nothing was evaluated, so I do not know what findings will appear. VND-001 and retention are not covered, and several PHI fields are not checkable without touching unrelated tables.
